title: U.S. Biomedical High-Altitude V-2/Aerobee Rocket Positive-Event Calibration Set
purpose: Freeze four NASA-documented U.S. biomedical high-altitude rocket events inside the JANUS study window before inspecting Blue Book or POSS-I overlap.

authority.primary: NASA — A Brief History of Animals in Space
authority.supporting: NASA History — Animals in Space collection and Project Mercury chronology
authority.population_warning: NASA explicitly states that its Animals in Space collections are not meant to be exhaustive. Therefore this artifact is a positive-event calibration manifest only and cannot define no-launch dates or a complete biomedical-launch denominator.

events.payload: Albert IV, rhesus monkey with monitoring instruments
events.source_semantics: NASA identifies this as the last V-2 monkey flight; the flight itself was successful, but the animal died on impact.
NASA states a V-2 launched on this date carrying a mouse; the animal did not survive impact after parachute/recovery failure.

events.location: Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico, USA
events.source_semantics: NASA records successful recovery of the monkey and 11 mice after the Aerobee flight.

events.payload: Patricia and Mike, two Philippine monkeys, plus Mildred and Albert, two mice
events.location: Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico, USA
events.source_semantics: NASA states the animal section was safely recovered by parachute after the high-altitude Aerobee flight.

population_semantics.allowed_role: Independent positive-event spatial/temporal and observation-opportunity calibration only.

bluebook_direct_attribution_requires: witness geography compatible with New Mexico launch/trajectory context
within-day ordering compatible when times are recoverable
narrative morphology compatible with a brief rocket/high-altitude luminous event
poss_direct_attribution_requires: Palomar actually observed the event date/time window
plate field and launch/trajectory apparent geometry are plausibly compatible
candidate morphology is not inconsistent with a moving or brief luminous human-made source

forbidden: No use of dates absent from this NASA collection as no-launch dates.
No rate/enrichment inference from this four-event positive-only set.
No direct attribution from civil-date coincidence alone.
No outcome-dependent expansion of this frozen calibration set.
